speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where your wrist pain is located and how long you have had the fever and skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, have you noticed any red, expanding "bull's-eye" rashes on your skin? Also, have you felt any tingling or weakness in your face or limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those lesions on your wrists and hands are very specific and concerning. Do you have any pain in your large joints like your knees, and have you noticed any eye redness or discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists are highly characteristic of Spotted Fever Group Rickettsia, particularly given your recent camping trip in Minnesota. I need to rule out other causes, so have you noticed any headache, nausea, or sensitivity to light?

REQUEST TEST: CBC
REQUEST TEST: Rickettsial Serology
REQUEST TEST: Joint Aspiration

speaker: Doctor
text:
The joint aspiration revealing Gram-negative diplococci strongly suggests Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which aligns with your sexual history and the pattern of migratory arthritis. Do you have any discharge from your penis or pain with urination?

REQUEST TEST: NAAT for Gonorrhea

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive NAAT confirms gonorrhea, and the Gram-negative diplococci in the joint fluid point to disseminated gonococcal infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI)
